questions.question: Which suture material is non-absorbable?
questions.explanation: Absorbable sutures are used for tissues that heal quickly (e.g. subcutaneous, bowel).
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Lignocaine (lidocaine) acts by:

options.A: Blocking voltage-gated sodium channels in nerve fibres

questions.explanation: Adrenaline prolongs its action; not used in end arteries.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The ASA physical status classification grades:
questions.explanation: ASA I is a healthy patient; ASA V a moribund patient.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Prophylaxis against deep vein thrombosis in surgical patients includes:

options.C: Early mobilisation, compression stockings and low-molecular-weight heparin

questions.explanation: Risk assessment guides prophylaxis.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The most important measure to reduce surgical site infection is:

options.A: Aseptic technique with appropriate antibiotic prophylaxis
options.D: Shaving the site the night before

questions.explanation: Hair removal by clipping, not shaving.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The WHO analgesic ladder starts with:

options.B: Non-opioids such as paracetamol and NSAIDs

questions.explanation: Step 2 weak opioids; step 3 strong opioids.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The most serious complication of transfusion of ABO-incompatible blood is:
questions.explanation: Stop the transfusion immediately and give supportive care.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Malignant hyperthermia is triggered by:

options.A: Volatile anaesthetics and succinylcholine in susceptible patients

questions.explanation: Treated with dantrolene.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which pain is typical of renal colic?

options.A: Severe colicky loin-to-groin pain with restlessness
options.B: Constant epigastric pain relieved by food

questions.explanation: Haematuria is common; imaging is by CT KUB.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Acute diverticulitis most commonly presents with:

options.D: Left iliac fossa pain, fever and altered bowel habit

questions.explanation: Sigmoid colon is the commonest site.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Bright red painless bleeding per rectum during defecation is characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Anal fissure causes painful bleeding.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: An anal fissure is characteristically:

options.B: Painful, worse during and after defecation, usually in the posterior midline

questions.explanation: Treat with fibre, topical GTN or diltiazem.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The commonest type of gallstone is:
questions.explanation: Risk factors: female, fat, fertile, forty.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: After abdominal surgery, early ambulation helps by:

options.B: Reducing chest and thromboembolic complications and promoting bowel function

questions.explanation: Encourage walking on the first post-operative day.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: An ileostomy typically produces:

options.A: Liquid, enzyme-rich output requiring a protective appliance

questions.explanation: Colostomy output is more formed.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The commonest type of hiatus hernia is the:
questions.explanation: Associated with GERD.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: An underwater-seal chest drain should always be kept:

options.A: Below the level of the patient's chest
options.C: Above the level of the chest

questions.explanation: Never clamp a drain draining a pneumothorax.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The most important management in rib fractures is:

options.B: Adequate analgesia to allow deep breathing and coughing

questions.explanation: Prevent pneumonia and atelectasis.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Flail chest is defined as:

options.B: Three or more adjacent ribs fractured in two or more places

questions.explanation: Causes paradoxical movement of the segment.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A thyroglossal cyst moves:
questions.explanation: It lies in the midline of the neck.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Cleft lip repair is usually performed at about:
questions.explanation: Palate repair at 6–12 months.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A comatose patient with a head injury should have the neck:

options.C: Immobilised until cervical spine injury is excluded

questions.explanation: A third of severe head injuries have cervical spine injury.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The Garden classification is used for fractures of the:
questions.explanation: Garden I–II undisplaced; III–IV displaced.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A displaced intracapsular femoral neck fracture in an elderly patient is best treated by:
questions.explanation: To permit early mobilisation.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: An extracapsular (intertrochanteric) hip fracture is usually treated by:

options.B: Internal fixation with a dynamic hip screw or intramedullary nail

questions.explanation: The blood supply is intact, so union is good.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which structure is at risk in fracture-dislocation of the knee?
questions.explanation: Check distal pulses after knee dislocation.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A fall from a height resulting in heel pain should prompt suspicion of a:

options.A: Calcaneal fracture, and look for associated lumbar spine fracture

questions.explanation: Bohler's angle on X-ray.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A Lisfranc injury involves the:
questions.explanation: Missed injuries cause chronic midfoot pain.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A Monteggia fracture-dislocation consists of:

options.C: Fracture of the proximal ulna with dislocation of the radial head
options.D: Fracture of the distal radius with dislocation of the DRUJ

questions.explanation: Galeazzi is the radius fracture with DRUJ dislocation.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A Galeazzi fracture is a fracture of the:

options.A: Radial shaft with dislocation of the distal radioulnar joint
options.C: Ulnar shaft with radial head dislocation

questions.explanation: ‘Fracture of necessity’: usually needs ORIF.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A Smith's fracture is:

options.B: A distal radius fracture with volar displacement (reverse Colles)
options.C: A distal radius fracture with dorsal displacement
options.D: A fracture of the ulnar styloid

questions.explanation: Caused by a fall on the back of the flexed wrist.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A Barton's fracture is:

options.B: A fracture of the radial head
options.C: An intra-articular fracture of the distal radius rim with carpal subluxation

questions.explanation: Unstable and usually treated surgically.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A radial head fracture usually results from:

options.D: A fall on the outstretched hand with the elbow extended

questions.explanation: Elbow aspiration relieves pain; early mobilisation is advised.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Olecranon fractures are typically treated with:
questions.explanation: To counter triceps pull.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Fractures of the surgical neck of the humerus are at risk of injury to the:
questions.explanation: Also posterior circumflex humeral artery.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In the three-column theory of Denis, an unstable spinal fracture involves failure of at least:
questions.explanation: Anterior, middle and posterior columns.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A Chance fracture is a:

options.D: Flexion-distraction injury of the thoracolumbar spine, often from seat-belt injury

questions.explanation: Associated with intra-abdominal injuries.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A fracture of the odontoid peg of C2 is typically seen in:

options.D: Hyperflexion injury with possible atlantoaxial instability

questions.explanation: Type II (base) has a high rate of non-union.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A Jefferson fracture is a:

options.C: Burst fracture of the ring of C1 caused by axial loading

questions.explanation: Caused by diving into shallow water.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A hangman's fracture is a:

options.D: Bilateral fracture through the pars interarticularis of C2

questions.explanation: Hyperextension with distraction.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Osteoarthritis is characterised pathologically by:

options.D: Progressive loss of articular cartilage with osteophyte formation

questions.explanation: Weight-bearing joints are most affected.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Rheumatoid arthritis is primarily a disease of the:
questions.explanation: Chronic synovitis with pannus formation.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In a child with a hot, swollen, painful joint, fever and refusal to bear weight the diagnosis must be:
questions.explanation: Urgent aspiration and antibiotics; hip is commonly involved.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The earliest movement lost in tuberculosis of the hip is:

options.D: Extension and rotation (flexion remains until later)

questions.explanation: Night cries are common in the early stage.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Avascular necrosis of the femoral head is associated with:

options.C: Steroid use, alcohol, sickle cell disease and trauma

questions.explanation: Ficat staging; MRI is the most sensitive test.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Osteochondritis dissecans most commonly affects the:

options.D: Medial femoral condyle of the knee

questions.explanation: Fragment of subchondral bone and cartilage may become a loose body.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Scheuermann's disease is:

options.D: Juvenile kyphosis with wedging of three or more adjacent vertebrae

questions.explanation: Increased thoracic kyphosis in adolescents.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Osteopetrosis (marble bone disease) is due to defective function of:
questions.explanation: Dense but brittle bones; fractures and bone marrow failure.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Achondroplasia is characterised by:

options.D: Short limbs with a normal trunk, inherited as autosomal dominant

questions.explanation: FGFR3 mutation.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Multiple myeloma typically produces on X-ray:

options.D: Punched-out lytic lesions of the skull

questions.explanation: Bence-Jones protein in urine and raised ESR.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which primary tumours most commonly metastasise to bone?

options.B: Breast, prostate, lung, kidney and thyroid

questions.explanation: Prostate metastases are sclerotic.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Chondrosarcoma characteristically affects:

options.A: Adults over 40 years, commonly pelvis and proximal femur

questions.explanation: Arises from cartilage; resistant to chemotherapy.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A non-ossifying fibroma is usually:

options.A: A benign asymptomatic eccentric metaphyseal lesion found incidentally in children

questions.explanation: Typically regresses spontaneously.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The radiological appearance of fibrous dysplasia is:
questions.explanation: Shepherd's crook deformity of the proximal femur.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The commonest brachial plexus birth injury is:
questions.explanation: Associated with shoulder dystocia and macrosomia.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Posterior dislocation of the hip may injure the:
questions.explanation: Peroneal division is more susceptible.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A patient with femoral nerve palsy has difficulty:
questions.explanation: Loss of sensation over the anterior thigh and medial leg (saphenous).
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Radial tunnel syndrome causes:

options.B: Lateral forearm pain over the supinator without sensory loss

questions.explanation: Often mistaken for tennis elbow.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Meralgia paraesthetica is due to compression of the:

options.D: Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve of the thigh

questions.explanation: Tingling and numbness over the anterolateral thigh.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Tarsal tunnel syndrome involves compression of the:

options.A: Posterior tibial nerve behind the medial malleolus

questions.explanation: Burning pain in the sole and heel.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The definitive treatment of acute compartment syndrome is:
questions.explanation: Release all tight bandages first.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Prophylaxis of heterotopic ossification after hip surgery includes:
questions.explanation: Vigorous passive stretching may provoke it.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A high tibial osteotomy is performed to:

options.A: Correct varus deformity and offload the medial compartment of the knee

questions.explanation: Used in young active patients with unicompartmental OA.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Arthrodesis is:

options.A: Surgical fusion of a joint to relieve pain

questions.explanation: Used in the ankle, wrist, spine and thumb.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The Ilizarov technique is used for:

options.B: Limb lengthening and deformity correction using a circular external fixator

questions.explanation: Based on distraction osteogenesis.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Apley's System of Orthopaedics and Fractures (chapter-level reference)
